rfm_tuples.R: 10-K MD&A: 'We expect our rig count in the United States will average 120 rigs in the first quarter [of 2024]. ... Based on contracts in place in the United States as of February 14, 2024, we expect an average of 79 rigs operating under term contracts during the first quarter of 2024 and an average of 52 rigs operating under term contracts during 2024.'
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — Verify against Q1 2024 10-Q (filed 2024-05-06) actual operating days and segment disclosure; Mode B — derive: if 79 of 120 rigs are on term contracts in Q1 but only 52 are contracted for FY24, ~27 rigs / ~22% of fleet rolls off term coverage during the year.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Q1'24 actual U.S. operating days = 11,024 over 91 days = 121.1 rigs/day — matches the 120 guide (PASS on Mode A). Mode B finding: drilling backlog at 3/31/24 = $527M with only ~14% reasonably expected to remain at 3/31/25 — confirms steep term-contract roll-off baked into the disclosed numbers. Average revenue/operating day fell from $36.28 (Q4'23) to $35.68 (-1.7% q/q), implying spot-market pricing pressure as term rigs convert to spot.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Headline rig-count guide PASS, but Mode B reveals the term-contract waterfall (79 → 52 during 2024, $527M backlog with only 14% lasting >12 months) is the real operational signal — pricing softens as rigs reprice to spot. Management discloses honestly but the framing is optimistic; the embedded term-coverage decline is a forensic finding that warrants moderate underdelivery on FY24 day-rate trajectory.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K Note on Goodwill: 'Based on the results of the goodwill impairment tests, the fair values of the drilling products, completion services, and cementing services reporting units exceeded their carrying values by approximately 4%, 11%, and 80%, respectively. Accordingly, no impairment was recorded for any of the reporting units.'
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — Verify the 4% cushion in the Q1 2024 10-Q goodwill commentary; Mode B — derive: a 4% fair-value cushion on the drilling-products (Ulterra) reporting unit means a sustained drop in oil/gas prices, rig count, or discount-rate creep would force an impairment trigger.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Cushion confirmed in 10-K text. Q1'24 10-Q states: 'During the first quarter of 2024, we determined there were no events that would indicate the carrying value of goodwill may not be recoverable.' Henry Hub spot gas closed at $1.50/MMBtu on 2/20/24 (10-K text) vs $2.74 Q4'23 average — i.e. gas prices ALREADY fell ~45% from the assessment date but management asserts no triggering event. Ulterra goodwill is exposed to global rig count which fell modestly. Drilling-products demand 'expected to remain steady through the first' quarter — Q1'24 10-Q discloses drilling products op income of only $6.5M on $90M revenue, implying ~7% segment op margin which is thin given the $27M of segment D&A.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Most important Mode B finding: a 4% cushion is functionally a 'next quarter could impair' disclosure that the company frames as 'no impairment recorded.' The gas-price collapse from Q4'23 ($2.74) to mid-Feb 2024 ($1.50) is acknowledged in the 10-K text but not re-applied to the Ulterra goodwill cushion. Standard forensic interpretation: Ulterra goodwill is a live impairment candidate within 2-3 quarters absent a gas-price recovery.

rfm_tuples.interpretation: Disclosure is accurate and the trajectory (declining concentration) is genuine — though Mode B clarifies the dilution is acquisition-mechanical, not customer-win-driven. No deception. Net forensic read: customer concentration is moderate (14%) for an oilfield services company and declining; not a red flag.

rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — Verify covenant text (total debt/cap ≤ 50%), current compliance, and the April 2024 maturity extension; Mode B — derive: is the 'amendment' a distress signal (extension granted because needed) or a routine kick-the-can (extension granted because economics favorable)?
rfm_tuples.M_value: Total debt $1.242B (Q1'24, ~flat to $1.243B Q4'23). Revolver $0 drawn, $548M capacity. Total debt-to-capitalization (using debt ~$1.24B / equity $4.75B = ~21% gross; debt/(debt+equity)) is ~21% — covenant headroom to 50% is comfortable. April 5, 2024 amendment 'increased' (per XBRL pten:RevolvingCreditFacilityMaturityDateTwoMember tag) and extended commitments — this is an upsize/extension, not a distress amendment. Senior notes structure: 3.95% 2028 ($482M) + 5.15% 2029 ($345M) + 7.15% 2033 ($400M) — well-laddered, no near-term wall.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Capital structure is investment-grade-style: low leverage (~21% debt/cap vs 50% covenant), zero revolver draw, $548M dry powder, no maturity wall before 2028. The April 2024 amendment is an upsize/extension done at the borrower's option, not a covenant-relief amendment. Direct contrast to the AAP-template distress pattern (sequential covenant loosening) — PTEN's amendment is a positive credit signal.

rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — Verify the buyback authorization increase and Q1 execution against the treasury-stock roll-forward table; Mode B — derive: is the buyback funded by operating cash flow or by drawing the revolver / issuing debt? Cross-check insider Form-4 selling against the same window.

rfm_tuples.M_value: Q1'24: Treasury repurchases under buyback program = 8,354,902 shares for $94.4M (avg $11.30/share). $945M remaining authorization at 3/31/24. Mode B insider cross-check: CEO Drummond (0001209191-24-004219, 3/4/2024) sold 253,260 shares at $11.73-$11.76 (~$2.97M); Director Cepak (0001209191-23-...) sold 15,000 at $11.78 in Dec 2023. rfm_tuples.interpretation: Buyback is funded organically (PASS on Mode A) but Mode B reveals a textbook tell: company is buying back stock at $11.30 average while the CEO is simultaneously SELLING ~$3M of personal stock at the same price, and zero insiders are buying despite the 29% drawdown. The classic interpretation is that management's revealed preference (buybacks at $11 average) does not match insiders' personal capital allocation. Not fraud, but a credibility ding — if management were truly convinced of undervaluation they would be buying personally.

supplemental_signals.auditor: PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP (PCAOB ID 238), tenure since 1993 — Big 4, 31 years, clean unqualified opinion, clean ICFR attestation
supplemental_signals.going_concern: No going-concern or substantial-doubt language anywhere in the 10-K or Q1 10-Q
supplemental_signals.covenant_status: In compliance with 50% debt-to-capitalization covenant at all measurement dates; actual ratio ~21%. Revolver $0 drawn, $548M available. No covenant amendments to relieve distress; April 2024 amendment was an extension/upsize.
supplemental_signals.debt_maturity_wall: Earliest senior note maturity: 2028 ($482M at 3.95%). Equipment loans $14.7M due 2025. No near-term refinancing risk.
supplemental_signals.insider_form4_window: 11/2023-5/2024: open-market sales 268,260 shares (CEO Drummond 253K @ ~$11.74 on 3/4/24; Director Cepak 15K @ $11.78 on 12/5/23). Open-market BUYS: 0. Other Form-4 activity is tax-withholding (F-code) and equity grants (A-code).
supplemental_signals.liquidity: Cash + revolver capacity ~$548M+ (cash position not separately extracted) vs $1.24B total debt. Q1'24 OCF $365.9M (+56% YoY); FCF $139M comfortably covers $130M Q1 capital return.
supplemental_signals.concentration: Top customer 14% of revenue (vs 18% in 2022) — declining (M&A-mechanical dilution).
supplemental_signals.goodwill_cushion: Drilling products (Ulterra) reporting unit: 4% fair-value cushion at 12/31/23 — IMPAIRMENT CANDIDATE if gas prices sustained at $1.50 or below. Completion services: 11% cushion. Cementing: 80% cushion.
supplemental_signals.key_acquisitions: NexTier merger closed 9/1/2023 (~$1.5B in stock); Ulterra acquisition closed 8/14/2023 — both still in purchase-price-allocation finalization; both are sources of the 4% / 11% goodwill cushion exposure.

summary: PTEN is an investment-grade-style oilfield services major with PwC auditor since 1993, clean ICFR, no going-concern flag, ~21% debt-to-cap vs 50% covenant, $548M undrawn revolver, $1.24B laddered debt with no maturity wall before 2028, and Q1'24 OCF +56% YoY at $366M. This is NOT a lying-distressed name. The forensic flags are forward-business-quality: (1) only 4% goodwill cushion on the Ulterra reporting unit against a gas-price collapse from $2.74 to $1.50/MMBtu disclosed in the same filing, (2) term-contract rig coverage waterfalls from 79 (Q1'24) to 52 (FY24 avg), and (3) the CEO sold ~$3M of stock at $11.74 on 3/4/24 while the company simultaneously executed $94M of buybacks at the same price — credibility ding with no insider buys during a 29% drawdown. The 29% drawdown looks more like a cyclical-down + gas-price + dilution-from-stock-deal reaction than a disclosure-quality problem. Verdict: NEUTRAL with mild lean to LONG-tier on honesty-alpha framework — the company is not lying; the drawdown reflects honest disclosure of a soft cycle.
verdict: NEUTRAL (lean LONG-tier on honesty-alpha): no lying detected, clean auditor + clean covenants + organic capital return, but Mode B flags two live goodwill impairment candidates and weak insider-buy signal that keep this off a high-conviction LONG basket.
